headline: Voting is your formal voice—the mechanism that translates individual preference into collective decision
universal_truth: Your vote is small individually but essential collectively; democracy works when people participate
fun_facts: Many elections have been decided by tiny margins—sometimes a handful of votes
Voter turnout varies enormously—from over 90% in some countries to under 40% in others
People fought and died for voting rights that many now take for granted
discussion_questions: Do you vote regularly? Why or why not?
How do you decide who to vote for?

hook.title: Welcome
hook.script: One voice among millions—does it matter? Your vote alone rarely decides anything. But democracy isn't about one vote deciding; it's about everyone's voice counting. Voting is how preference becomes policy.

options.text: I want to learn something new
options.response: Perfect. Curiosity is the first step to understanding. Let's explore this together.
That curiosity is exactly what we need. Let's dive in and discover something amazing.

cliff.title: The Question
cliff.script: One vote rarely changes outcomes. So why bother voting?

options.text: Voting matters collectively, not individually—if everyone thought their vote didn't matter, democracy would collapse; voting is citizenship in action, not just personal calculus
options.response: Yes. Democracy is a collective action problem. Each vote is small, but together they create mandate. Your vote matters because enough people voting is how democracy works at all.
Expression is part of it, but voting is more than feeling—it's participating in actual decisions...

q1.title: Informed Voting
q1.script: Voting without information is noise, not signal. Know what you're voting on. Research candidates and issues. An informed vote contributes more than an uninformed one.
q1.prompt: What's your first impression of "Informed Voting"?

options.text: This confirms what I already knew
options.response: Great foundation! Now let's build on that knowledge with something you might not expect...
Perfect starting point! This insight will connect to even more surprising facts ahead.

q2.title: Barriers to Voting
q2.script: Not everyone can vote easily. Registration, access, time off work—barriers exist. Some are practical; some are deliberate. Removing barriers strengthens democracy.
q2.prompt: How does this connect to what you already know?

options.response: Exactly. These connections are how knowledge becomes understanding.

options.text: I need to think about this more
options.response: That's a good instinct. Deep understanding takes time. The next fact will help clarify.

q3.title: Beyond Elections
q3.script: Voting happens beyond elections: in organizations, communities, informal groups. The skill of participating in collective decisions applies everywhere. Practice it.
q3.prompt: What surprises you most about this?

options.text: I never thought about it this way
options.response: That shift in perspective is exactly the point. New angles reveal new truths.
That's learning in action. When understanding shifts, you're really getting it.

wisdom.title: Today's Wisdom
wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: Your vote is small individually but essential collectively. Democracy works when people participate. Use your voice.
wisdom.prompt: What resonates most with you today?

options.response: That central truth will stay with you. Let it guide your thinking.
Application is where knowledge becomes wisdom. That's the real learning.

outro.title: See You Tomorrow
outro.script: That's Day 334—November complete! Tomorrow begins December, and we'll explore how groups make rules. Until then, consider how you use your voice.
outro.prompt: Before you go—what will you take from today?

options.response: Reflection deepens learning. Let these ideas simmer in your mind.
Teaching others is the best way to learn. You've already begun the ripple.

growTrack.title: Voting Commitment - Will You Use Your Voice?
growTrack.activity: Do you vote regularly? Are you registered? Do you research before voting? Make a commitment: What will you do to ensure you're an informed, participating voter?
